name: KY-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 district with incumbent Morgan McGarvey seeking re-election
McGarvey's roughly $1.9 million cash advantage against a challenger with no reported fundraising
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at 98 percent
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race
model.rationale: The district's ten-point Democratic lean, McGarvey's overwhelming financial edge, and market pricing near 98 percent all point the same direction, and nothing in the available evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for Maria Rodriquez or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow the margin, though an upset would require an unusual reversal.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan McGarvey, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election with the advantages typical of a safe seat. The Louisville-area district leans Democratic by about ten points, and the broader picture adds a favorable political environment, the value of incumbency, and a large financial edge. McGarvey has raised roughly two million dollars and holds nearly all of it on hand, while Republican Maria Rodriquez shows no reported fundraising in the available record.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the assessment rests on district fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near ninety-eight percent. The expected margin is around twenty-one points, with meaningful uncertainty because direct polling evidence is absent. For an upset, Rodriquez would need outside money and an environment shift well beyond anything currently visible; the seat remains firmly in the Democratic column.
